display.title: The Secret Chuppah at Rabbi Levi Yitzchak's Home (Chof Av)
display.summary_short: At a children's Chof Av farbrengen: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak, the Rebbe's father, holds a secret midnight chuppah in Soviet Russia, and the building manager who spied on him becomes a baal teshuvah.
display.summary_long: Recorded live at a children's farbrengen on the eve of Chof Av, the yahrzeit of the Rebbe's father. The storyteller explains that he was named Levi after Rabbi Levi Yitzchak, then tells a story from Soviet Russia. Rabbi Levi Yitzchak, known as Reb Leivik, teaches Torah and mitzvos to Jews all over his city, and the police pay the manager of his apartment building to report on every visitor. Late one night, during the curfew, an old woman knocks gently at his door and kisses the mezuzah. Her daughter, who works in a Communist office, is marrying a Jewish co-worker, and they have agreed to a Jewish wedding only if it is done in secret. Reb Leivik slips through the alleyways to gather a minyan, but only nine come. Rather than call a man he suspects is a spy, he knocks on the building manager's door and invites him as the tenth. After the chuppah and the refreshments Rebbetzin Chana prepares, the manager stays behind, hands over his secret police card, and asks to learn Torah. The storyteller closes with the lesson of Ahavas Yisroel and listening to parents, and the children sing a nigun.
display.lesson: Like Rabbi Levi Yitzchak, care for every Jew and spread Yiddishkeit; we are free to learn Torah and do mitzvos with simcha, and our only opponent is the yetzer hara.
